rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window, retain early compounds, and ensure strongly retained compounds elute. This scouting run will identify critical pairs before narrowing the gradient and testing slope or temperature.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the crowded early triplet responds to slope. The comparison will distinguish slope-sensitive separations from pairs needing temperature-driven selectivity changes.
The shallower gradient improved the early triplet but incurred a substantial time penalty. Return to the faster gradient and test higher temperature for improved selectivity and shorter retention.

Higher temperature leaves only one under-resolved pair and provides nearly two minutes of retention-time headroom. A moderately shallower gradient tests whether that pair can reach baseline resolution while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a steeper gradient instead. This should improve that pair and shorten retention, while checking whether neighboring separations remain adequate.

Slope changes alone have not resolved the remaining pair. Raise the starting organic fraction to shift selectivity in the early cluster, using a 12-minute gradient to preserve separation of its other neighboring pair.

Raising phi0 improved the critical pair from 1.09 to 1.33 without compromising other separations. Test one further grid step to seek full resolution while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.
Injection 7 reached the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while retaining injection 7 as the benchmark.
The 10-minute gradient retained full resolution and maximum CRF. Test the next shorter duration to locate the speed limit, with injection 8 available if either early critical pair falls below 1.5.

The 8-minute broad gradient narrowly missed full resolution, so reduce its steepness by lowering phi1 to 0.85. This intermediate slope should restore both critical pairs while remaining faster than injection 8, with the final peak still inside the gradient.

Injection 10 is now the fastest fully resolved method tested. Test a higher starting organic fraction against injection 8 to see whether further window trimming can shorten retention without compressing the early peaks below R = 1.5.

Higher phi0 compromised another early separation, so retain the fastest fully resolved gradient window. Test a 5 C temperature decrease to measure local selectivity changes and determine whether temperature offers room for further shortening.

The temperature decrease worsened both critical separations, favoring 60 C. Test the intermediate endpoint between injections 9 and 10 to determine whether full resolution can be retained at a last-peak time below 6 minutes.

The fastest fully resolved method remains injection 10, and nearby slope changes have bracketed its resolution limit. Test the low-temperature extreme for a different elution-order pattern that might open another selectivity window for fast separation.

Low temperature produced extensive co-elution, so return to 60 C and refine the successful window. Lowering phi1 one step from injection 10 should increase the critical-pair margin while keeping retention shorter than the fully resolved 10-minute gradient.

Trim the high-organic portion of the program while retaining a slope between the fully resolved injections 10 and 15. The last peak is expected near the gradient end, so this tests a shorter programmed gradient without sacrificing the early critical separations.

Test whether a shallower gradient restores the early pair compromised at phi0 = 0.20 in injection 11. This explores an alternative fully resolved window below the 10-minute scoring threshold, while injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten the newly resolved phi0 = 0.20 method by one grid step to bracket its minimum viable gradient duration. Injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method and already achieves the maximum CRF.

Return to the faster phi0 = 0.15 window and increase phi1 one step from injection 16. This tests a slope between injections 10 and 13, potentially shortening the fully resolved separation below 6 minutes, though the critical pair is near its resolution limit.

Injection 19 still has a pair below 1.5 despite its rounded CRF of 1.000, so injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method. Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 7 to increase resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test whether the higher starting fraction and shallower gradient can compensate for the selectivity loss at 55 C, yielding a fully resolved lower-temperature alternative within 10 minutes. Injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Injection 21 narrowly missed full resolution despite its rounded score. Lower phi1 one step to make the gradient slightly shallower, aiming to resolve that pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Return to the faster 60 C window and lower phi1 one step from injection 16 to strengthen the critical separation while reducing organic usage. The final peak may enter the hold, so this run will establish whether the narrower endpoint remains practical without a time penalty.

Use the same initial gradient slope as fully resolved injection 10, but end the gradient earlier and elute the late compounds during the hold. This tests whether a four-minute programmed gradient can retain maximum CRF; the main risk is increased retention of the final peak.

Finish with a narrowed window and a slope expected to provide more resolution margin than injection 10 while keeping all peaks inside the gradient and below 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already secured; injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
